defects.summary: First user message loses its text part when an image attachment is present. The OpenAI request body carries content=[{type:image_url}] with NO {type:text} part, so the mock's lastUserText is '' and every retry returns E2E04-FALLBACK. The UI still renders the typed prompt (it is stored client/server side), but the model never sees it.
defects.evidence: captureBodies run: all 9 turn-1 request bodies have messages[1].content parts=['image_url'] only (passing runs have ['text','image_url']); see e2e04-result.json mockState.bodies from the 10:08/10:10 diagnostic runs (superseded by final result.json; bodies were captured in-run). Server-side builder is src/hc/server/model_adapter/request.clj ->user-message: TextContent is only emitted when (context-text message) is non-blank, so (:text message) was blank at request build time -> race between text persistence and attachment send.
defects.hypothesis: optimistic/async message entity: attachment send path can reach the model adapter before :text (or :content) is populated on the message record.

defects.summary: The app JVM exits cleanly ~90s uptime into every run that survives the first turns. GC log shows orderly gc,exit at uptime 93.855s with heap healthy (288M/385M committed, NO heap dump, NO OutOfMemoryError, server log has no error). Client sees ws reconnect ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED -> 连接状态：连接中断 -> 材料库未就绪; branch prompt never reaches the mock.
evidence: error-context.md aria snapshot: 连接状态：连接中断; 当前轮仍在生成 stuck
standalone probe (node startApp, no browser, no model traffic): app stayed healthy 150s+ -> death is triggered by test activity, not a timer
app.mjs JVM_OPTS include -XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError but no OOM occurred; orphan-watchdog ruled out (JVM parent is the node runner, not a shell; shell-launcher? false)
defects.openQuestion: what delivers the orderly shutdown at ~90s under load: SIGTERM from an external reaper, an in-app supervisor/maintenance path (restore-supervisor stop-current!), or a shutdown-hook trigger inside a component (scheduler/fleet/materials). GC exit logging proves signal-or-System/exit, not a crash.
